findings.issue_text: [Medium/api] common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoProvider.java:~45 — `order()` is added as an abstract method to a ServiceLoader-discovered SPI, breaking compatibility: any third-party CryptoProvider implementation compiled against the previous interface will fail to compile or throw AbstractMethodError at runtime when the new comparator in detectProvider invokes order(), breaking crypto initialization entirely; it should be a default method (e.g., `default int order() { return 0; }`).

[Medium/security] common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoIntegration.java:~56-70 — detectProvider no longer fails when multiple providers are found: all in-tree server providers (default, elytron, FIPS) return order() == 200, so ties are resolved by ServiceLoader/classpath order, meaning a deployment with both FIPS and non-FIPS provider jars can silently start with the non-FIPS provider (previously an IllegalStateException failed fast); the 'Ignored crypto providers' information is only logged at DEBUG so the misconfiguration is invisible in production logs, and any lower-order provider already on the classpath gets silently disabled just by adding authz-client.

[Low/bug] authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:~110 — in concatenatedRSToASN1DER, the two standalone ASN1Encoder.create().write(...) calls build encoders whose output is immediately discarded (leftover from refactoring); this dead code allocates unnecessarily and misleads readers, and both lines should be removed.

[Low/api] authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:~50 — getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the JDK's default KeyStore provider (e.g., SUN), which is not BouncyCastle, violating the interface contract; callers relying on BC-specific algorithms or keystore types (BCFKS, BC PBE schemes, etc.) will fail or silently behave differently, and unlike the other unimplemented methods that throw UnsupportedOperationException, this fails in a much harder-to-diagnose way.

[Low/bug] authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/ASN1Decoder.java:~62-71 — readInteger() does not validate readLength()'s return value: a zero-length INTEGER (e.g., crafted input `30 04 02 00 02 00`) reaches new BigInteger(new byte[0]) and throws NumberFormatException, and an indefinite-length (0x80) value would be passed to read(-1) causing NegativeArraySizeException — unchecked runtime exceptions instead of the declared IOException on malformed input.

[Low/test_gap] authz/client/src/test/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/test/ECDSAAlgorithmTest.java:~52-62 — the test only asserts DER→concat→DER→concat round-trip equality and never verifies the converted output is a cryptographically valid signature (e.g., signature.initVerify(keyPair.getPublic()); signature.verify(asn1Des)); symmetric conversion errors (r/s transposition or byte-order mistakes applied consistently in both directions) would pass the test while producing invalid signatures.

[Low/bug] authz/client/pom.xml:~68-72 — the org.hamcrest:hamcrest test dependency is unused: the new test only uses org.junit.Assert, and JUnit 4 already pulls hamcrest transitively, adding a needless and potentially version-conflicting test classpath entry.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/security] common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoIntegration.java:~56-70 — detectProvider no longer fails when multiple providers are found: all in-tree server providers (default, elytron, FIPS) return order() == 200, so ties are resolved by ServiceLoader/classpath order, meaning a deployment with both FIPS and non-FIPS provider jars can silently start with the non-FIPS provider (previously an IllegalStateException failed fast); the 'Ignored crypto providers' information is only logged at DEBUG so the misconfiguration is invisible in production logs, and any lower-order provider already on the classpath gets silently disabled just by adding authz-client.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes CryptoIntegration.detectProvider to no longer throw when multiple CryptoProvider implementations are found; it now sorts by CryptoProvider::order descending and returns the first, only logging the rest at DEBUG (common/.../CryptoIntegration.java). In-tree providers DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, and FIPS1402Provider all implement order() and each returns 200 (diff shows all three), so when more than one is on the classpath the selection becomes dependent on ServiceLoader/classpath iteration order rather than a deterministic preference, whereas previously it failed fast via IllegalStateException. This can silently select a non-FIPS provider when a FIPS provider is also present, with no production-visible log by default.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/ASN1Decoder.java:~62-71 — readInteger() does not validate readLength()'s return value: a zero-length INTEGER (e.g., crafted input `30 04 02 00 02 00`) reaches new BigInteger(new byte[0]) and throws NumberFormatException, and an indefinite-length (0x80) value would be passed to read(-1) causing NegativeArraySizeException — unchecked runtime exceptions instead of the declared IOException on malformed input.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `ASN1Decoder.readInteger()`, it calls `int length = readLength();` and then unconditionally does `byte[] bytes = read(length); return new BigInteger(bytes);`. From the diff, `readLength()` explicitly returns `-1` for indefinite-length encoding (`length == 0x80`), which would be passed to `read(-1)` and cause `new byte[-1]` → `NegativeArraySizeException` (unchecked). Also, if `length` is `0`, `read(0)` returns an empty array and `new BigInteger(new byte[0])` throws `NumberFormatException` (unchecked). Both cases contradict the method’s `throws IOException` contract and result in runtime exceptions on malformed ASN.1 input.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] authz/client/src/test/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/test/ECDSAAlgorithmTest.java:~52-62 — the test only asserts DER→concat→DER→concat round-trip equality and never verifies the converted output is a cryptographically valid signature (e.g., signature.initVerify(keyPair.getPublic()); signature.verify(asn1Des)); symmetric conversion errors (r/s transposition or byte-order mistakes applied consistently in both directions) would pass the test while producing invalid signatures.

adjudication.rationale: The newly added ECDSAAlgorithmTest only checks that conversions are internally reversible: it signs data to get an ASN.1 DER signature (`sign`), converts DER→RS-concat (`rsConcat`), converts back RS-concat→DER (`asn1Des`), then converts again and asserts `rsConcat` equals `rsConcat2`. It never verifies that `asn1Des` is a valid signature over the original data with `keyPair.getPublic()`. As the finding states, a symmetric mistake in both conversion directions (e.g., swapping r/s or consistent byte-order issues) could still satisfy the round-trip assertion while producing an invalid DER signature. This is a specific, diff-grounded test gap for the new crypto conversion logic, not a runtime defect by itself.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an explicit test dependency on `org.hamcrest:hamcrest` in `authz/client/pom.xml`, but the only new test (`ECDSAAlgorithmTest`) imports/uses `org.junit.Assert` and does not reference Hamcrest APIs. This makes the added direct Hamcrest dependency appear unnecessary and could introduce avoidable test classpath/version management complexity (especially since JUnit commonly brings Hamcrest transitively).
